thread:
sophia: heads up — hitting weird propagation lag on private VPC canary slices. single canary slice took ~3m to apply across air-gapped nodes, while control-plane shows it committed immediately. :thinking:
michael: got logs? is this the same cluster that had the heartbeat jitter last week?
sophia: collecting. console shows rollout slice weights updated (50% -> 10%) but agent reports still on old config for a few agents. most agents reconcile within 10s but ~6 nodes stayed on old for minutes.
emily: any commonality between those 6 nodes (region, image version, agent version)?
sophia: quick check: all are on the older side (agent v2.3.1) and are in the customer-prem rack behind a NAT gateway. several had intermittent TCP resets in system logs.
raj: plausible — air-gapped setups rely on a push fanout from controlplane -> site-proxy -> agents. if the site-proxy queued requests and retried with long backoff, that could explain stagger. we should confirm queue/backoff metrics.
michael: can you paste the rollout policy config used? might be something with the apply window or stagger settings.
sophia: here it is (redacted):
```yaml
rollout:
  mode: canary
  slices:
    - id: slice-1
      weight: 5
      apply_timeout: 2m
      guard:
        error_rate_threshold: 1.5
    - id: slice-2
      weight: 95
      apply_timeout: 2m
```
(sorry for quick snippet)
raj: apply_timeout is per-slice at control-plane level, but agents have their own reconcile window (agent.reconcile.max_jitter). if the agent jitter is large, control plane thinks it applied but nodes may be waiting random jitter up to configured max. check agent config.
emily: also remember we have a 'deferred-ack' path for air-gapped where agents ack locally and proxy forwards later — if proxy had a backlog it delays final manifest propagation. we had a related incident doc last year.
sophia: checking agent configs now. noticed nodes with lag also had reconcile_jitter set to 180s (default override).
michael: that's the smoking gun. for private installs we lowered jitter historically to smooth HA, but someone bumped it via deploy-tooling.
emily: propose short-term mitigation: detect slices where > max_stale_seconds and pause rollout + alert; long-term: expose reconcile_jitter in Console per-customer and surface a warning when it's above rollout.apply_timeout.
sophia: agree. can we add a quick guard in control-plane: if observed agent-ack delay distribution P90 > apply_timeout, auto-pause and add annotation to rollout?
raj: doable — control-plane already collects agent-heartbeats and ack latencies. adding a threshold check is ~2 days of work (backend + tiny UI). for emergency, we can add a runtime flag to enable the pause heuristic.
michael: also add a telemetry tag to those rollouts (private=true, airgapped=true) so we can query trends. we need to know if this is one-off or systematic.
emily: I'll prototype Console banner copy: "Detected high agent reconcile jitter — recommended: set agent.reconcile.max_jitter <= 30s for canary rollouts". keep it actionable.
sophia: thanks team. I'll roll a small fix: runtime flag + alert rule to pause if P90_ack > apply_timeout. will post PR link.
deploy-bot: noticed rollout/2026-04-15-sophia-canary started for customer-id 6789 (private). status: partial-applied -> paused by operator.
michael: perfect — watch the dashboards for that customer. I'll run a one-off script to scan other private installs for reconcile_jitter > 60s and ping infra owners.
emily: quick follow-up: can we also make the UI show 'expected worst-case propagation' per-customer given their agent_jitter and proxy backlog? customers keep asking for a single number.
raj: yes — we can compute expected propagation = max(agent_jitter_p90, proxy_queue_time) * num_retries (approx). will add to backlog.
sophia: ok closing loop: short-run: runtime flag + alert + PR. long-run: UI exposure + telemetry + docs update. thanks. :white_check_mark:
